chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding the erroneous killing resembling the deliberate — namely killing with a whip, a stick, or rocks — that the wergild for that is made severe. It is one hundred camels, among which are forty pregnant she-camels (khalifa) ranging from a thaniyya (six-year-old) to a bazil of its year (nine-year-old), and thirty hiqqas (four-year-old she-camels), and thirty bint labuns (three-year-old she-camels).

And for the purely erroneous (killing), there should be thirty hiqqas, and thirty bint labuns, and twenty bint makhaz (two-year-old she-camels), and twenty male ibnu labuns (three-year-old male camels). And the value of each camel in silver is one hundred and twenty dirhams, or ten dinars; and from sheep, the value of each old she-camel (nab) from the camels is twenty sheep.

key_terms.الْخَطَأُ: Purely erroneous killing — accidental without intent; carries the standard diyya distribution
key_terms.الْخَطَإِ شِبْهِ الْعَمْدِ: Quasi-intentional manslaughter — killing with a normally non-lethal instrument; carries heavier diyya
key_terms.بَازِل عَامِهَا: Bazil of its year — a nine-year-old camel that has broken its last molar
key_terms.بِنْتَ لَبُون: Bint labun — a three-year-old she-camel whose mother has given birth again
key_terms.ثَنِيَّة: Thaniyya — a six-year-old she-camel that has entered its sixth year
key_terms.حِقَّة: Hiqqa — a four-year-old she-camel; a common diyya category
key_terms.خَلِفَة: Khalifa — a pregnant she-camel; the most valuable category in diyya
key_terms.دِيَة: Diyya — blood money; financial compensation paid to the victim's family in lieu of retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between quasi-intentional and erroneous killing in Shia jurisprudence, and how is the diyya calculated?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a ruling of Imam Ali (as), as reported by Imam Sadiq (as), distinguishing between two categories of unintentional killing in Islamic law: quasi-intentional manslaughter (khata' shibilh al-'amd) — where the killer used a non-lethal instrument like a whip, stick, or stone — and purely erroneous killing (khata'). The wergild (diyya) for quasi-intentional killing is heavier and specified entirely in terms of female camels of older ages, while the diyya for erroneous killing includes a broader mix of camel categories. The hadith also provides monetary equivalents for those unable to pay in camels.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the erroneous (killing) resembling the deliberate, if he kills with the whip, or with the stick, or with the rocks.

The wergild of that is harsh, and it is one hundred from the camels in which there are forty ‘Khalifat’ what is between a ‘Saniya’ (six years old) to ‘Bazil’ (nine years old), and thirty ‘Hiqqa’ (four years old), and thirty ‘Bint Laboun’ (three years old female).

And for the erroneous (killing) there should be thirty ‘Hiqqa’ (four years old), and thirty ‘Bint Laboun’ (three years old), and twenty ‘Ibnat Makhazin’ (two years old females), and twenty ‘Ibn Laboun’ (three years old males), and the value of each camel in terms of foliage is one hundred and twenty Dirhams, or ten Dinars; and from the sheep, the value of each sheep, for every camel is twenty sheep’.
